From January 3 to June 5, 2012, voters of the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ chose its nominee for ___E:president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ in the ___E:2012 United States presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ won the Democratic Party nomination by securing more than the required 2,383 ___E:delegates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delegate_(American_politics))___ on April 3, 2012, after a series of ___E:primary elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partisan_primary)___ and ___E:caucuses U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caucus)___ .

He was formally nominated by the ___E:2012 Democratic National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Democratic_National_Convention)___ on September 5, 2012, in ___E:Charlotte, North Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte,_North_Carolina)___ .

The general expectation was that, with President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ having the advantage of ___E:incumbency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incumbency)___ and being the only viable candidate running, the race would be merely ___E:pro forma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_forma)___ .

Independent progressive Vermont senator ___E:Bernie Sanders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders)___ reportedly considered challenging Obama in the primaries but decided not to run after then-Senate Majority Leader ___E:Harry Reid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Reid)___ talked him out of it (He would later run unsuccessfully for the Democratic nomination in ___E:2016 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders_2016_presidential_campaign)___ and ___E:2020 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders_2020_presidential_campaign)___ ).
Several of the lesser-known candidates made efforts to raise visibility.
Some ___E:Occupy movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupy_movement)___ activists made an attempt to take over the Iowa caucuses,  and got about 2% of the vote for Uncommitted.

With nine minor candidates on the ballot in New Hampshire, there was a debate at ___E:Saint Anselm College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Anselm_College)___ in ___E:Goffstown, New Hampshire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goffstown,_New_Hampshire)___ on December 19, 2011,  in which seven candidates participated. ___E:Anti-abortion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-abortion)___ activist ___E:Randall Terry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randall_Terry)___ bought time on television in order to show graphic commercials denouncing ___E:abortion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion)___ .
Three candidates – other than Obama – who had been on the ballot in New Hampshire were also on the ballot in Missouri.

One such candidate, Randall Terry, attempted to air graphic TV commercials during ___E:Super Bowl XLIV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLIV)___ , but was met with resistance from various TV stations   in some locations.

The ___E:Democratic National Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Committee)___ also tried to stop the ads by claiming that Terry was not a legitimate Democratic candidate even though he was legally on the ballot.

A number of partisans of ___E:Barack Obama citizenship conspiracy theories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_citizenship_conspiracy_theories)___ , challenging the legitimacy of Obama's ___E:birthright citizenship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birthright_citizenship_in_the_United_States)___ , attempted to have the President's name removed from the Georgia primary ballot.
A state administrative judge upheld a ___E:subpoena U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subpoena)___ , which was ignored by the President and his staff.

In February 2012, the activists' legal challenge was rejected by a Georgia state law judge and by the ___E:Secretary of State of Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_State_of_Georgia)___ , and Obama remained listed on the primary ballot.

On May 8, 2012, ___E:Keith Russell Judd U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Russell_Judd)___ , an inmate serving a 17.5-year sentence, won 41% of the primary vote in West Virginia against incumbent ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ , a higher percentage of the vote in one state than any other primary opponent of Obama had hitherto achieved in 2012.   Shortly thereafter, attorney ___E:John Wolfe, Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wolfe,_Jr.)___ won 42% of the primary vote in Arkansas after widespread speculation that Wolfe could possibly pull off an upset of the state.

Challengers to President Obama only qualified for the ballot in eight states – New Hampshire, Missouri, Oklahoma, Louisiana, Texas, West Virginia, Arkansas, and Alaska – while a ninth (Ohio) was going to have Randall Terry on the ballot, but removed his name before the ballots were printed.
Randall Terry also attempted to contest the Kansas caucus, but was denied a spot on the caucus ballot after the state's Democratic Party determined that he didn't meet the requirements.
Darcy Richardson suspended his bid for the nomination on April 28, 2012. He still appeared on the ballot in Texas and was an eligible write-in candidate in California after suspending his campaign.
Four states canceled their respective Democratic primaries altogether, citing Obama being the only candidate to qualify on their respective ballot: Connecticut,  Delaware,  New York,  and Virginia.

Despite the limited opposition and ultimately receiving 100% of the pledged delegates, Obama's total percentage of the national popular primary vote was the lowest of any incumbent since the contested ___E:1992 election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_presidential_primaries,_1992)___ when ___E:George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ was challenged by ___E:Pat Buchanan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Buchanan)___ .
Even without any clear candidate opposition, Obama faced a considerable amount of resistance in several southern states such as Arkansas, Oklahoma and Kentucky.
None of the three had been contested by the same anti-Obama candidate, yet ran significant margins, to the point some speculated he would lose these contests.
Obama was on the ballot in all states, where he ran mostly unopposed.

The number of pledged delegates allocated to each of the 50 U.S. states and ___E:Washington, D.C. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___ is based on two main factors: (1) the proportion of votes each state gave to the Democratic candidate in the last three presidential elections, and (2) the number of electoral votes each state has in the ___E:United States Electoral College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Electoral_College)___ .

In addition, fixed numbers of delegates are allocated to ___E:Puerto Rico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico)___ , ___E:American Samoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Samoa)___ , ___E:Guam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam)___ , the ___E:U.S. Virgin Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Virgin_Islands)___ , and ___E:Democrats Abroad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democrats_Abroad)___ under the party's delegate selection rules.

Depending on each state's law and each state's party rules, when voters cast ballots for a candidate in a presidential caucus or primary, they may be voting to actually award delegates bound to vote for a particular candidate at the state or national convention ( binding primary or caucus), or they may simply be expressing an opinion that the state party is not bound to follow in selecting delegates to the national convention ( non-binding primary or caucus).
States are awarded bonus pledged delegates if they schedule their primary or caucus later in the primary season.
Those states with April dates are awarded a 10 percent increase, while those who schedule from May 1 to June 12 get a 20 percent increase.
And starting on March 20, a 15 percent bonus is awarded when clusters of three or more neighboring states begin on the same day.

The unpledged ___E:superdelegates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superdelegate)___ included members of the ___E:United States House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ and ___E:Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ , state and territorial ___E:governors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_United_States_Governors)___ , members of the Democratic National Committee, and other party leaders.
Because of possible deaths, resignations, or the results of intervening or special elections, the final number of these superdelegates was not known until the week of the convention.
Some delegates committed to candidates other than the President were not permitted to be elected in contested primaries for administrative reasons.
